title.ko: used to · would · be / get used to
title.en: used to · would · be / get used to

explain.ko: used to + 동사원형은 지금은 하지 않는 과거의 습관이나 상태를 말합니다. would + 동사원형도 반복된 과거 행동에 쓸 수 있지만 상태(live, have, be)에는 쓰지 않습니다. be used to + -ing / 명사는 '~에 익숙하다', get used to + -ing / 명사는 '~에 익숙해지다'로, 형태는 비슷하지만 뜻이 전혀 다릅니다. 부정과 의문은 did / didn't + use to입니다(Did you use to …?).
explain.en: Use used to + base verb for past habits or states that are no longer true. Would + base verb can also describe repeated past actions, but not states (live, have, be). Be used to + -ing / noun means 'be familiar with', and get used to + -ing / noun means 'become familiar with'. They look similar but mean something completely different. Questions and negatives use did / didn't + use to (Did you use to …?).

head: 표현 / Structure
의미 / Meaning
예문 / Example
rows: 예전 습관·상태 / past habit or state
I used to live in a village.
반복된 과거 행동 / repeated past action
Every summer we would go to the beach.
I'm used to getting up early.
I'm getting used to my new job.

notes.ko: 상태에는 used to만 씁니다: I used to have a dog (would 불가).
notes.en: For states only used to is possible: I used to have a dog (not would).

notes.ko: be used to 뒤에는 -ing형이 옵니다: used to cooking.
notes.en: After be used to use the -ing form: used to cooking.

notes.ko: 부정과 의문에서는 use가 되고 -d는 사라집니다: Did you use to …?
notes.en: In questions and negatives it's use to, not used to: Did you use to …?

items.passage:
STORY OF THE VILLAGE MUSEUM
This building used to be a railway station. Ten trains passed through every day, and in summer tourists would queue to get on. When the railway closed in 1985, the building stood empty for a while. Today it is a museum telling the history of the village.
